- **A CLICK MOVES NOTHING EXCEPT THE THING THAT WAS CLICKED — and this is a RULE, not a list of bugs.** The bar entry above is one instance of it; Court raised it a second time about a different surface ("opening the whole doc note moves the cards on the right"), and the audit that followed found two more nobody had reported. The general form has three parts and every one of them is load-bearing. **A disclosure COVERS, it does not DISPLACE.** The whole-document panel was `static` between a sticky bar and `body > main`, so opening it inserted a quarter of a screen into the layout: the document's top went 55.39 → 282.91 and every anchored card followed the mark it hangs on, one of them straight past the fold cap and off the rail. The settled region at the rail's foot had the same shape for a different reason — the rail was then a flex column whose height the viewport fixed, so a list opening at the FOOT took its height out of the band ABOVE it: the bottom fold cluster and its three clamped cards rose 225.69px and `document.elementFromPoint` at the clicked coordinate returned `.gly-card-note`. The panel floats to this day, `fixed` off the bar's measured height (`--gly-bar-h`, published by `App.watchBar`; the bar's height is not a constant and must not be guessed). **THE RAIL'S TWO DISCLOSURES DO NOT, ANY MORE, AND THAT IS THE STRONGER FORM OF THE SAME RULE.** They were `absolute` at `bottom: 100%` of their own head, opening upward over the map; they are ordinary blocks that open BELOW their head now, because the rail scrolls with the document and there is no fixed band for them to take height out of. Settled and changed are the last two sections of the rail in that order, so opening one displaces the one below it and nothing else, and opening the last displaces nothing at all — the head the cursor is resting on never moves either way. `just motion` asserts it directly (the list's top is at or below its head's bottom, no card in the map moves, the head is still under the cursor) and DECLARES the one box that does change: `#gly-rail`'s own, which is the sum of its sections and grows downward. A float was the right answer to a question that no longer exists, and keeping it would have been the second system this whole regroup was about. Covering some prose or some cards while open is the ordinary behaviour of a disclosure and is NOT the popup §5 forbade — nothing has to be dismissed before a comment can be typed, focus is not trapped, and Esc closes it the way Esc closes every other surface. **A READOUT THAT PUSHES A BUTTON IS THE SAME DEFECT AS A BUTTON THAT PUSHES ITS NEIGHBOUR.** The bar has ONE flexible cell and it sits between the readout and the controls: `.gly-doc · .gly-census · #gly-status · .gly-seal · .gly-spacer · .gly-collapse · .gly-mode · .gly-hold · #gly-revise · .gly-seal-actions` (read off the DOM 2026-08-16 — `just layers` §1d prints it as a note now, because three documents had the tail wrong in the same order and each reader copied the last one). What is a RULE is the position of the flexible cell: readouts before it, controls after. The order WITHIN the control group is not a rule, it is a consequence — `makeCollapse` and `makeMode` both `insertBefore` `#gly-revise`, and collapse is constructed first. There were THREE readouts in that region and there is one — `#gly-editor-status` (`connected · saved …`), `.gly-census-untracked` (the standing sentence) and `#gly-status` (the reply to a press) all carried the same `flex: 100 1 0` yield, so they shortened together and Court read `your edits…`, `connected …`, `revision r…` off the bar: three fragments of three sentences is less information than one sentence, and it is the rail's own incoherence one surface over. `entry.js`'s `paintReadout` composes them into the SHELL'S `#gly-status` (the element that exists before the bundle runs, carries the live region, and is what `edit.html` writes `editor bundle missing` into), NEWEST CLAUSE FIRST — reply · connection-if-bad · saved · the standing sentence — because the cell ellipsizes at its END, so the order IS the truncation policy and the last clause has to be the one whose loss costs least. The reply stays a FIELD (`this.said`, written only by `say`) rather than a second box, which is the same guarantee the two elements existed for: a poll cannot swallow the only feedback Revise gives. A SEALED page prints only what the seal said — `your edits apply` is false of a document that is not editable — and the element is NOT hidden, because a reopen's reason lands in it. `#gly-status` used to be AFTER the spacer, so the one word it prints in reply to a click slid `.gly-collapse`, `.gly-mode` and `.gly-hold` 59px; the census goes BEFORE the readouts and not merely before the spacer, because it carries three controls of its own and the naive order slid them 140.89px. **A LABEL THAT CHANGES ON ITS OWN CLICK IS THE THIRD FORM, AND THERE WERE THREE MORE OF THEM.** `.gly-collapse` (`⇥` → `⇤ notes`, 38.44 → 89.02px, and the second click landed on `.gly-bar` with the button no longer under the cursor), `#gly-revise` (`Revise` → `revising · 0s`, 80.58 → 139.58px, and then a further 8.44px at every decade of the counter with no click at all), and `.gly-census-overall`, whose count changes when a note is filed in the panel it opens. Same answer as hold's every time: both labels in ONE grid cell, or a reserve stated as a BOUND (`4ch` of seconds, `16ch` of handle — it was `28ch` while the label read `▾ 99 notes on the whole doc`, and the reserve was retuned WITH the label, which is what a bound stated against a specific label pair obliges) and said out loud to be one. `web/motion.mjs` is the pass, `just motion` runs it, and `docs/superpowers/plans/no-motion-on-click-e2e.md` carries the measurements and the two exemptions that were declared rather than fixed — chief among them that a card whose note slot fills grows and slides the cards below it, because the alternative is reserving that line on every card forever and the band already chose sliding over overlapping.
